Still pretty good! The only reason I wouldn't put it higher is, because Risk of Rain Returns just added on every aspect of it without getting rid of any features in the original.

Years ago I bought this game to play with friends, and knew relatively little about it, so we quickly dropped it after discovering how brutally difficult it is. However, I decided to pick it up again recently to see if I could manage to get to the end of the game, and after getting past the fairly steep learning curve, I started to have more fun and did manage to finish a few runs. The game definitely isn't perfect, but I think it's still worth picking up, as long as you're prepared for the initial challenge.

The basic gameplay loop has you trying to survive a given area while collecting upgrades until you find a teleporter which sends you to the next area (after surviving a wave of enemies). The longer you stay alive however, the harder the enemies you encounter get, so it's a race against the clock to get stronger faster than your enemies. Unfortunately, you start the game with only a single character unlocked, no artifacts, and none of them can be unlocked on the easiest difficulty. The character you start with isn't the strongest one either, and as mentioned, this game is pretty unforgiving, so it makes it really difficult to learn. However, once you play it for a number of hours and start getting the hang of it, you'll eventually reach the point where you unlock more characters and artifacts (which are pretty fun to hunt for), and many of these make the game significantly easier. Once you get a run going, the game is pretty exciting as well. It's pretty fun to start collecting a huge horde of items and go from struggling to survive to melting everything in sight.

The game looks alright, although the visuals can definitely be a bit small and hard to see at times, especially when there's a lot of things going on on screen at one time. The game isn't bug free either, and I ran into a number of issues, including a fairly clunky menu system that sometimes requires you to use keyboard and mouse (which was a bit frustrating when playing on my Steam Deck), UI that sometimes didn't show up where expected in multiplayer, and an online multiplayer system that seems to be completely broken.

[b]TL;DR[/b] This is a fun, but brutally difficult roguelike that is very difficult to learn, but is quite enjoyable if you're willing to put the initial effort in. Despite some issues with the clunky menu system making it a bit hard to play on my Steam Deck, some issues with the UI, and an online multiplayer system that doesn't seem to work, I'd still recommend the game if you enjoy roguelikes and you're looking for a challenge.
